import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report is done; now checking precedent in the research repo for how earlier linkers published embedded copy-ready guides.

Report read. Diagrams status is `none`, so no proposed figures to place. Now checking the infographic and link targets.

Infographic confirmed beside the report. Next: snapshot the source to a scratch file and build the restructured note from it programmatically so content stays byte-exact.

Structure planned. Building the restructured note from exact source slices.

Draft built. Now validating: line-level inventory diff against the source, anchors via pandoc, and fence counts.

Inventory matches: all 48 table rows, 22 fence lines, and the one Mermaid diagram are intact; only the intended heading, link, and opening changes differ. Checking anchors with pandoc.

All eight in-document anchors resolve. Final checks, then writing the file without overwrite.

The file is written and registered. Finishing the turn through `/sase_final`.

I published the lead's report as the canonical note, `202611/private_event_notes_how_to/private_event_notes_how_to.md`. It is registered as `research:202611/private_event_notes_how_to/private_event_notes_how_to.md` (`file:explicit:9fd996ac0ccf7b57d00cac47`). The commit declaration was accepted, and the host commits the research repo after this turn.

**How it opens:** title, a one-sentence research query, the infographic (`private_event_notes_how_to_infographic.png`, which I confirmed sits beside the report), then **Bottom line**.

**How it's organized:** Bottom line → What ships today versus what the guide assumes → The copy-ready guide → Why the guide looks like this → Accuracy rules the editor must keep → Verify before publishing → What stays out of the guide → Where the reports disagreed → Method and sources. The lead's opening "Research request / Lead researcher" block, with the evidence pins, now sits at the start of Method and sources. I added eight in-document links, for example from the bottom-line bullets to the status table, the disagreement table and the guide's figure.

**Diagrams:** none were added. The image agent's `diagrams` status was `none`: it considered 19 candidates and rejected all of them. So there was no manifest to read and the file has no figure blocks. The lead's own Mermaid figure ("When does a private event note reach the Event Task?") is still there, unchanged.

**Changes inside the embedded guide:** the guide is a draft of a page meant for the bob-cli docs, and this document has different rules, so three things changed in it:
- **Heading levels:** its headings sit two levels lower here (its `#` title became `###`, its sections became `####`), because the file may have only one `#` title.
- **Step numbers:** "1." to "4." were removed from the step headings. The PDF renderer numbers headings itself, so hand numbers would print twice.
- **Links:** the five links to other docs pages (six occurrences) were written relative to `docs/guides/` in bob-cli, so they don't resolve from the research folder. I pointed them at bob-cli GitHub links pinned to the lead's evidence commit, `ffcb9864`. I checked in the bob-cli checkout that all five files and both anchors exist at that commit.

Because of these changes, the published note is not a paste-ready copy of the docs page. The exact copy-ready source is still in `private_event_notes_how_to__final.md`, which I didn't touch.

**Checks:**
- **Content:** every line of the lead's report appears in the new file except the intended heading, link and opening changes. All 48 table rows and all code-fence lines are identical.
- **Links:** every in-document link resolves under `pandoc`. The lead's report contained no external URLs, and no link was dropped as unrepairable.

**Not embedded:** `lands.png`. It is one of the grk researcher's assets, which the lead only names as a folder path in Method and sources.
